prompt: Tutorial question 1. A proton enters a magnetic field of 0.5 T perpendicular to the field at 2 x 10^6 m/s. Calculate the magnetic force and the radius of its path. Take the proton mass as 1.67 x 10^-27 kg and its charge as 1.6 x 10^-19 C.
explanation: Perpendicular means θ is 90 degrees and sin 90 = 1, so the sine quietly disappears. Force: F = qvB = 1.6 x 10^-19 x 2 x 10^6 x 0.5 = 1.6 x 10^-13 N. Radius: r = mv over qB = (1.67 x 10^-27 x 2 x 10^6) / (1.6 x 10^-19 x 0.5) = 3.34 x 10^-21 / 8.0 x 10^-20 = 4.2 x 10^-2 m, which is about 4 cm. A believable size for a proton curving in half a tesla, which is the step 7 check.

why.b: Wrong on the radius by a factor of 100, a slip when dividing the exponents.
why.c: Wrong on the force, from halving it as though the sine were 0.5 rather than 1.
why.d: Wrong. 1.6 x 10^-19 is the proton's CHARGE copied out as though it were a force.
why.e: Wrong on both, from doubling the force and the radius together.

prompt: A proton moves with a velocity of 3.5 x 10^6 m/s in a magnetic field of 0.25 T at an angle of 60 degrees. Which component of the velocity sets the RADIUS of the helix, and which sets its PITCH?

options.text: v sin 60 sets the radius, and v cos 60 sets the pitch
v cos 60 sets the radius, and v sin 60 sets the pitch
v tan 60 sets the radius, and v sin 60 sets the pitch

explanation: Split the velocity into the part ACROSS the field and the part ALONG it. The perpendicular part, v sin θ, is what the magnetic force acts on, so it drives the circular motion and fixes the radius: r = mv sin θ over qB. The parallel part, v cos θ, feels no force at all, because sin 0 is zero along the field, so the proton simply drifts steadily in that direction, and that drift over one period is the pitch: p = v cos θ times T. Circle across the field, drift along it, and the two together trace a helix.

why.a: Correct. Sine for the radius, cosine for the pitch.
why.b: Wrong, and it is the trap, since these two are the easiest pair in the course to swap.
why.c: Wrong. Using the whole speed for both ignores that only the perpendicular part is deflected.
why.d: Wrong. If the pitch used sine too, the path would never advance along the field.
why.e: Wrong. A tangent does not appear anywhere in this topic.
